opening: A boy holds a gold stamp under the dead lamp. Mabry quietly puts the refund money back inside her sleeve.

trials.action: Turn the stamped face to the wick
trials.result: Gold scatters cold light across the wall. No writing appears underneath it.

trials.action: Slide the stallholder’s dated receipt into the lamp
trials.result: The wick burns steady beside the sale date. It cannot date the bowl.

admission: I bought my stall board one letter at a time. Today I could afford the Y in my name.

editions.action: Hang the receipt where buyers can lift it
editions.result: The boy checks the date himself. Mabry spends the morning explaining the other stamps.

editions.action: Give Mabry the lamp for her stall
editions.result: She lights each receipt before she takes a coin. The queue curls past her neighbour’s empty stall.

editions.action: Hold the lamp for Mabry while she shows the buyer
editions.result: Mabry turns the bowl herself. For once the person who sold the story has to stand in its light.

away.action: Light the margin on the Nile label
away.result: A second strip glows under the display heading. The date beside it belongs to the copy.

witnessOffer: Hold the lamp for Mabry while she shows the buyer
witnessResult: Mabry turns the bowl herself. For once the person who sold the story has to stand in its light.
guardianVoice: I can give light a weight, almost. I cannot weigh what it cost the boy to ask for his coin back.

opening: Marrow catches a loose reed in the door. Someone has rubbed a date from the paper where the fold hid it.

trials.action: Unroll the storekeeper’s copy
trials.result: Its last mark trails off the edge. The copyist never saw the end of the older roll.

trials.action: Hold the later delivery slip against the gap
trials.result: The later writer signs the delivery in full. Neither piece names the day the other was written.

admission: My father reads our case to visitors. I wanted him to get through a day without anyone laughing.

editions.action: Leave both rolls on separate pins
editions.result: Visitors can trace the broken line. Wystan sits by his father at opening time.

editions.action: Give Wystan a facsimile hinge to mend
editions.result: He can lift it to show the missing date. Anyone in a hurry sees a smooth label.

editions.action: Leave the later slip on Marrow’s high hook
editions.result: Wystan’s father can find the correction without a younger hand turning the roll for him.

away.action: Trace the loan number on the frozen page
away.result: The oldest shelf mark points to a later family amendment. Its signature survives on the reverse.

witnessOffer: Leave the later slip on Marrow’s high hook
witnessResult: Wystan’s father can find the correction without a younger hand turning the roll for him.
guardianVoice: I used to give the oldest reed the highest hook. Rain gets to the oldest reed first, too.

opening: A warm thumbprint blooms over a blank name in the ice. Mossgrave tries to close the lid on Odile’s hand.

trials.action: Catch the impression on the cold pane
trials.result: The blank has four square corners. A slip was lifted out after the page was numbered.

trials.action: Warm the flap with the family seal
trials.result: A closed envelope drops into Odile’s hand. The seal gives her family the choice of opening it.

admission: My little sister practised our name every night. She thought it would fit if she wrote small enough.

editions.action: Mark the missing slip on the public file
editions.result: Odile can point to what went missing. She must answer strangers at the desk.

editions.action: Let Odile hold the sealed envelope
editions.result: She keeps its contents private. The public file carries a gap and the date she took custody.

editions.action: Let the family lift the pane themselves
editions.result: Odile sets a tea towel across the envelope. Mossgrave warms one corner for her alone.

away.action: Hold still the scraped graduation on the tide drum
away.result: The gap stays white while the surrounding ink flows back. No reading was taken there.

witnessOffer: Let the family lift the pane themselves
witnessResult: Odile sets a tea towel across the envelope. Mossgrave warms one corner for her alone.
guardianVoice: Nobody told me how long a seed can sleep. I am still waiting for one my sister planted.

opening: Halcy’s tide globe spills a second blue shadow across the harbour plan. Astor has painted only one line on the bell card.

trials.action: Advance the tide wheel a notch
trials.result: The near berth dries before the slower boat can turn.

trials.action: Draw the wind vane across the same hour
trials.result: With a shore wind the second shadow slips over the ferry steps. Both traces fit the morning gauge.

admission: They used to ask my teacher what I had said while I stood beside him.

editions.action: Call the earliest safe tide by bell
editions.result: The small boats move. The deep boat loses an hour waiting for a second call.

editions.action: Pin both ghost tides at the landing
editions.result: Astor signs both curves. A deckhand stays to help passengers read them and misses his tea.

editions.action: Set a peg where the child can leave her shoes
editions.result: Astor makes a safe shelf for today. Tomorrow’s tide keeps both its shadows.

away.action: Cast the two wind paths across the bird net
away.result: One gust carries calls to the far recorder. A silent recorder need not mark an empty clearing.

witnessOffer: Set a peg where the child can leave her shoes
witnessResult: Astor makes a safe shelf for today. Tomorrow’s tide keeps both its shadows.
guardianVoice: I once told a child every height the water might reach. She was asking where to leave her shoes.

opening: Ninefold lands on the tally board in the shape of a question mark. Gale’s neat last column has no space for a call without a sighting.

trials.action: Count shadows at dusk
trials.result: One bird casts two shadows across the forked lamp. The moths count themselves until somebody laughs.

trials.action: Turn the screen to the dawn reeds
trials.result: A reply comes from below the blind. The sunlit count missed the nesting bank.

admission: If my numbers look soft, they will cut down my listening post. My brother built it high enough for me.

editions.action: Add a column for heard-only calls
editions.result: Gale keeps the nesting bank on the route. Comparing this year with last takes longer.

editions.action: Keep a parallel notebook for uncertain calls
editions.result: The annual count stays comparable. Gale takes a second round before going home.

editions.action: Give the dawn watcher a second slate
editions.result: Gale opens a line for a reply heard off the edge of the first count. The two watchers will meet at dusk.

away.action: Turn the many-eyed lens on the rejected sample tray
away.result: A sample too small for the jaw has been excluded from every figure on the guild sheet.

witnessOffer: Give the dawn watcher a second slate
witnessResult: Gale opens a line for a reply heard off the edge of the first count. The two watchers will meet at dusk.
guardianVoice: We counted my sister twice. It felt like having her back. Please keep the two numbers where we can see them.

opening: A hot sample rolls under Grisel’s boot. Harl’s form lists a guild recipe. The smith who taught it worked outside the gate.

trials.action: Quench twin slips with the same weight
trials.result: Changing just the cooling bath leaves a bend in only one slip.

trials.action: Repeat the cool bath in a different clamp
trials.result: The second slip bends at the jaws. The maker’s hands mattered along with the bath.

admission: I could get her method into the guild book. I could not get her through its front door.

editions.action: Leave room for the traveller’s account in the register
editions.result: A new shift can find its teacher. The guild buys fewer named batches until she returns.

editions.action: Demonstrate both clamps at the gate
editions.result: Buyers can repeat the test. Harl works his break to explain why the guild stamp stays.

editions.action: Put Grisel’s cold and warm strikes on the docket
editions.result: The guild copies two conditions onto its label. Harl sets a stool at the bench for the traveller.

away.action: Repeat a print with only the pressure changed
away.result: The missing word comes back without changing a single letter of type.

witnessOffer: Put Grisel’s cold and warm strikes on the docket
witnessResult: The guild copies two conditions onto its label. Harl sets a stool at the bench for the traveller.
guardianVoice: My elbow rings false when it is cold. I once failed a perfectly good hammer before breakfast.

opening: The twin printers catch opposite ends of a falling proof. Each recognises their own coffee ring. Liesl has already sold the next edition.

trials.action: Match the torn edge to the first forme
trials.result: A shop nick repeats on both copies. The nick places the shop but cannot tell the twins apart.

trials.action: Overlay the forgotten author’s correction
trials.result: One line was added in a different hand after printing. The late copy carries the stronger reading.

admission: If the press sleeps tonight, three families go without a shift tomorrow.

editions.action: Print the correction on the next run
editions.result: The new sheet names the reviser. Readers with an old sheet must come back.

editions.action: Send slips for readers to clip to existing copies
editions.result: People can mend the sheet they have. Somebody must keep the loose slips with it.

editions.action: Keep the two corrections facing each other
editions.result: The twins give one another the clean sides to sign. Liesl hangs both at the public press.

away.action: Overlay the harbour survey and the pilot’s soundings
away.result: An inlet appears under two spellings. Shared ink concealed two different survey dates.

witnessOffer: Keep the two corrections facing each other
witnessResult: The twins give one another the clean sides to sign. Liesl hangs both at the public press.
guardianVoice: I remember spilling the coffee. So does my brother. Would you turn the paper over for us?

opening: Old Saltmark sings a name beyond the edge of Penrose’s survey. An apprentice has already tied a mooring rope to the wrong blue peg.

trials.action: Steer by the printed sounding
trials.result: It clears the shoal on a falling tide. The far bank shares its printed name with the landing.

trials.action: Steer by the pilot’s sung turn
trials.result: The last verse finds the landing in fog. It carries no depth for the loaded boat.

admission: When our boat radio failed I could say only one name clearly. I wanted one word every crew could hear.

editions.action: Mark both names with the depth and date
editions.result: New crews have a common reference. Local pilots give up a private shortcut.

editions.action: Leave a blank with a call for a pilot
editions.result: The route stays under local care. Late boats may have to wait outside the channel.

editions.action: Leave space for the surveyor and the singer to sign
editions.result: Penrose reads each name back to its speaker. The two people disagree about where the reef ends.

away.action: Unroll the blank chart behind the scenery
away.result: The actor’s pencilled exit leads through a wing the front-row diagram leaves empty.

witnessOffer: Leave space for the surveyor and the singer to sign
witnessResult: Penrose reads each name back to its speaker. The two people disagree about where the reef ends.
guardianVoice: The first printed chart I ever saw had my sister’s reef on it. Somebody must have listened.

opening: Lucan hands out a programme headed REFUSAL. From the last seat the empty chair looks like a deliberate insult.

trials.action: Move the mask from prompt corner to balcony
trials.result: A crate hides the actor’s hand from the balcony. The first row saw a wave.

trials.action: Light the aisle behind the empty chair
trials.result: An usher lifts the chair for a late arrival. A single empty seat carried three different stories.

admission: An empty house sounds like somebody drawing a very long breath and never letting it go.

editions.action: Let the ushers print both sightlines
editions.result: Late arrivals have a way into the scene. Lucan loses the brisk heading that sold the first tickets.

editions.action: Open two seats at the dress rehearsal
editions.result: The audience can test its own reading. Two paying places stay empty every evening.

editions.action: Trade the prompt mask for the last spectator’s ticket
editions.result: Lucan sits in the seat he used to describe to other people. He crosses a word off the programme.

away.action: Listen to the bargain from the carrier’s seat
away.result: The clerk calls a net weight. From behind the full basket the carrier hears only the larger number.

witnessOffer: Trade the prompt mask for the last spectator’s ticket
witnessResult: Lucan sits in the seat he used to describe to other people. He crosses a word off the programme.
guardianVoice: I watched from the wings for thirty years before anyone offered me a seat. Which chair did they keep for you?

opening: Quarta sets three baskets on the brass hands. Cass puts a seal over the place where the wicker weight should go.

trials.action: Weigh the empty nesting basket
trials.result: Its double base weighs as much as a handful of grain.

trials.action: Swap wicker while keeping the grain
trials.result: The seal reads the same lot. The hand moves because the new basket is lighter.

admission: My mother taught me to keep the coins for flour apart from the coins for someone worse off. This week both jars are empty.

editions.action: Settle today’s sale by the tare
editions.result: The buyer recovers the difference. Cass must explain the refund before supper.

editions.action: Loan the check weight to both stalls
editions.result: Tomorrow’s customers can test the scale. Today’s receipt stays disputed.

editions.action: Hand the check basket to the customer
editions.result: Cass waits while a child steadies the brass hands. The queue watches the wicker tip the empty pan.

away.action: Set the fair weight against two water tokens
away.result: Each token buys a turn of the wheel. The higher bank receives less water in that turn.

witnessOffer: Hand the check basket to the customer
witnessResult: Cass waits while a child steadies the brass hands. The queue watches the wicker tip the empty pan.
guardianVoice: My left hand and my right agree to a grain. They have never had to buy a loaf.

opening: Brisk carries three cups through the spring and brings back two full. Dorran’s upstream and downstream crews signed on different days.

trials.action: Split one turn equally at the head gate
trials.result: The lower cup is short. Water soaks into the dry bank on its way down.

trials.action: Let the last crew call the gate change
trials.result: All three hear the turn. The first crew leaves its plot to stand by the gate.

admission: My sister and I used to sing across the weir. After the last public meeting she stopped answering.

editions.action: Bring both crews to the wet bank
editions.result: Everyone sees the shortfall. Dorran can no longer keep the two signatures a day apart.

editions.action: Send a cup and a witness each way
editions.result: The crews keep separate meeting places. The witnesses give up their next shift.

editions.action: Let the smallest crew sound the next turn
editions.result: The upstream crew hears its own gate discussed from downstream. Dorran leaves both meeting dates posted.

away.action: Follow the current between two district bins
away.result: Each bin is full on its own return. The travelling library sits between them without a booking.

witnessOffer: Let the smallest crew sound the next turn
witnessResult: The upstream crew hears its own gate discussed from downstream. Dorran leaves both meeting dates posted.
guardianVoice: Lull fell asleep at the meeting. Brisk called it agreement. Swirl kept his cup upside down till morning.

opening: Ledgerlock lifts a brass foot over the district line and stalls. Nyle’s rule has no square for a doorstep shared by two streets.

trials.action: Run the rule from the east entrance
trials.result: The household goes west on the list and waits for a cart that never comes.

trials.action: Move the starting peg to the west entrance
trials.result: The same household goes east. Each district has a justified entry, and neither delivers.

admission: Our street is quiet for the first time in years. I forgot quiet could sound exactly like being left out.

editions.action: Keep both route names and one shared stop
editions.result: Each district keeps its song. One driver waits for the other at the boundary.

editions.action: Leave the cart free to cross on request
editions.result: A household can call it across. Somebody who cannot call still needs a visitor.

editions.action: Walk the missed doorstep with its resident
editions.result: Nyle pencils in both entrances and initials the route change. The library arrives from the quieter street.

away.action: Open the date rule in the listening catalogue
away.result: Every unsigned account fell out at one step, including the one the volunteer heard herself.

witnessOffer: Walk the missed doorstep with its resident
witnessResult: Nyle pencils in both entrances and initials the route change. The library arrives from the quieter street.
guardianVoice: I can show every turn of my wheels. I still need a person to tell me whose house this is.

opening: Hollin lifts a hand at a footstep nobody else picked out. Tolly has clipped a family voice to the public copy of a walk.

trials.action: Listen from the bridge stair
trials.result: A second cane answers the first. The walker had company for this part.

trials.action: Follow the listener’s access slip
trials.result: One voice agreed to a family hearing. The public index lists the event without permission to play it.

admission: I hid my own family’s page first. After that, every empty space looked like a little kindness.

editions.action: Keep the voice in the family room
editions.result: The relative can hear both footsteps. Visitors get the signed index and a silence.

editions.action: Invite a fresh public telling of the walk
editions.result: The speaker can set their own boundary. A later account cannot replace this recording.

editions.action: Let the family choose the public pause
editions.result: Tolly keeps the private voice with the family. Visitors can still find the point at which the public take ends.

away.action: Hear the model maker’s uncredited assistant
away.result: She says which tray she watered twice. The harvest figure now has a witness and a limit.

witnessOffer: Let the family choose the public pause
witnessResult: Tolly keeps the private voice with the family. Visitors can still find the point at which the public take ends.
guardianVoice: I know that pause. I cannot tell you whose it is until they say I may.

opening: Tansy fits the last paper tree into the garden. Sabine brings a ribbon from a famous visitor. The model harvest fails on the shaded side.

trials.action: Run the dry slope with the same rain
trials.result: The low field keeps a crop. The higher bed dries before the fair.

trials.action: Add the narrow shade cloth and rerun
trials.result: The result changes along one row. The visiting expert never saw this run.

admission: People remember my face after a lecture. I wish somebody remembered the question I brought with me.

editions.action: Invite the gardener to demonstrate the shade
editions.result: A local finding travels with the model. Sabine gives up her place on the programme.

editions.action: Publish the model with its two trial runs
editions.result: A stranger can repeat the comparison. The gardener waits for a name on the public label.

editions.action: Leave the shade cloth in the gardener’s hands
editions.result: Sabine helps the gardener lift the cloth. Visitors can run either season and read who planted each row.

away.action: Run a miniature hearing with the quiet bench moved
away.result: A delegate who could not hear the first motion can now give a reason before the vote.

witnessOffer: Leave the shade cloth in the gardener’s hands
witnessResult: Sabine helps the gardener lift the cloth. Visitors can run either season and read who planted each row.
guardianVoice: I was going to put the blue ribbon on that row. My mother says the smallest tree is the only one that looks like home.
